title: Passing off vs trademark infringement - the difference that matters
p1:
Two businesses can be fighting over the same brand name, but the legal reason may be completely different.

Many people think trademark disputes are always about registered trademarks. That is where the confusion begins.
p2:
Trademark infringement usually happens when someone uses a mark that is identical or confusingly similar to a registered trademark without permission.

Passing off is different. It protects the reputation a business has built, even when there may be no registered trademark. A small local business with loyal customers can still take action if another person tries to copy its identity and mislead buyers.
p3:
The surprising part? A business does not always need a registration certificate to protect its goodwill. Reputation, customer recognition, and proof of confusion can matter greatly.

The practical takeaway: registration strengthens protection, but a brand’s reputation can also have legal value.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a business name, logo, or product that felt like it was copying another brand? Do you think reputation should receive legal protection even without registration?
